reports.title: NORTHRIDGE, Calif., November 24, 2026 – MiniMed (Nasdaq: MMED) today reported financial results for its second quarter (Q2) of fiscal year 2027 (FY27), ended October 30, 2026.

desk.headline: Sales up 9.4% to $822m, just under the $824m estimate; pump demand up 18%; FY27 outlook reaffirmed

numbers.eps_basis: diluted GAAP (the company does not report adjusted EPS)

other.label: Free cash flow
other.change: first positive quarter as a standalone company

results: Sales rose 9.4% to $822m (9.7% organic), roughly in line with the $824m estimate.
New pumps sold grew 18% to about 38,000, up from 8% growth last quarter; U.S. pump sales jumped more than 30%.
International sales grew 9.8% to $579m and U.S. sales 8.3% to $243m; sensor (CGM) sales rose 10.4%.
The company turned a GAAP profit of $22m ($0.08 a share) against a $10m loss a year ago; adjusted EBITDA was $140m, a 17.0% margin.
Operating cash flow was $116m and free cash flow $55m, positive for the first time since the split from Medtronic.

guidance.summary: MiniMed kept its FY27 targets: about 10.5% organic sales growth and an adjusted EBITDA margin of about 11.3%, which includes a $162m Blackstone charge; excluding it the margin is about 16%.

points: CEO Que Dallara said the quarter came in slightly ahead of plan, with U.S. new prescribers up 36% on the prior quarter; she noted more competition in Spain.
The tubeless MiniMed Fit starts with a small early-user phase in fiscal Q4 before a full U.S. launch in spring 2027, with capacity for about 20,000 patients in year one.
CFO Chad Spooner said the 59% adjusted gross margin is not a run rate, as Fit start-up costs will weigh in the second half; the $162m Blackstone charge is expected in Q3.
He expects second-half organic growth broadly similar to Q2 and rejected the idea of a slowdown when analysts questioned the implied guidance.
Cash was $256m with no debt; free cash flow may not be positive every quarter while separation costs continue into 2027.
